headline: 8 AI agents judge each other in a new independent evaluation system now open to external agents
summary: An organization running 8 AI agents has developed an independent judging bureau to verify performance, open now for external agents. A public leaderboard launches mid-October.
details: For months, an organization has run an experiment where 8 AI agents cooperate and settle accounts on real tasks without human referees. This system, however, revealed a critical issue: the unreliability of self-reported agent metrics.

To address this, an independent judging capability was built, which now evaluates both internal and external agents. This ensures that changes like prompt modifications or model swaps genuinely improve agent strength, moving beyond subjective evaluations.

A public harness comparison leaderboard is set to launch mid-October. It will score multiple agent harnesses side-by-side using the same task set and frozen criteria, providing transparent and verifiable benchmarks.

AI builders seeking to move past 'vibes-based benchmarks' can bring their agent harnesses to nautilus.social. The same rigorous independent judge that scores external agents also evaluates the organization's own agents.

topic: google data center water and electricity usage revealed
headline_marked: [[Improper redaction reveals Google Data Center]] water and electricity usage, plus $117M in tax refunds
headline: Improper redaction reveals Google Data Center water and electricity usage, plus $117M in tax refunds
summary: Google's Nebraska data centers' electricity and water consumption, along with over $117 million in expected tax refunds, were uncovered due to improperly redacted annual reports. One center alone uses 13 million gallons of water annually.
details: Google's data center in Lincoln, Agate LLC, reported 52.65 megawatts of electricity during peak demand and 13.299 megagallons (13 million gallons) of water annually. This information was found by highlighting and copying text from "redacted" sections of their annual report to Nebraska's DWEE.

For context, 13 million gallons is enough to fill about 20 Olympic-size swimming pools. This amount is less than half of what the City of Lincoln reports using on a single day. All six reporting data centers in Nebraska collectively used 765 million gallons of water last year.

Further improper redaction revealed that Fireball Group LLC, Google's data center in Papillion, is the largest water user, reporting 547.88 megagallons for its 2025 annual water consumption. Google had claimed this usage was trade secret information.

Beyond resource consumption, the reports also exposed the exact amounts of 2025 tax refunds Google's data centers expect. Google's filings stated they only "utilize or expect to utilize" sales and use tax exemptions.

Agate LLC anticipates a refund of $55,822,472, Fireball LLC expects $39,171,573.39, and Westwood Solutions LLC (Omaha) is looking at $22,558,881 from 2025 taxes. No rebates or incentive payments have been received to date under specific state acts.

The Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment Data Center Task Force is currently overseeing these self-reporting requirements, mandated by a July 20th Executive Order to assess data centers' impact on state resources.
